_note: US insurance product taxonomy — each entry classifies the product as an Insurance Contract (mortality/morbidity risk) or Investment-Type Contract (deposit-type), with explicit guidance mapping to SSAP / ASC standards.

products.name: Term Life Insurance
products.brief_intro: Term life provides a death benefit if the insured dies within a fixed coverage period (typically 10-30 years). Pure protection product — no cash value accumulates. Premiums are level for the initial term and re-rate to attained-age rates thereafter.
products.description: Term life is the most economical permanent-mortality-risk transfer vehicle. Insurers price using mortality tables, persistency assumptions, and a target investment yield. Post-LDTI (ASC 944 / ASU 2018-12), the liability for future policy benefits is measured at cohort level with annual unlocking and an upper-medium-grade A-rated discount. Statutory reserves follow VM-20 PBR under SSAP 51R.
key_features: Level premium for initial term (e.g., 10, 20, 30 years)
Death benefit only — no cash value or surrender benefit
Convertibility option to permanent life (term-conversion features)
Re-entry/renewability at attained age after term expires
products.market_note: US in-force face amount approximately $850B+ on term blocks across major carriers

products.name: Whole Life Insurance
products.brief_intro: Whole life provides lifetime mortality coverage with a guaranteed cash-value buildup and (for participating contracts) annual policyholder dividends. Premiums are level for life. The contract combines pure mortality risk with a guaranteed-interest savings element.
products.description: Issued primarily by mutual insurers (Northwestern Mutual, MassMutual, New York Life, Guardian), participating whole life pays annual dividends out of divisible surplus, sourced from favorable mortality, expense, and investment experience. Cash-value accumulates on a guaranteed basis with a contractual minimum interest rate. Reserves follow VM-20 PBR (SSAP 51R) or pre-2017 commissioners' reserve methods.
products.market_note: US in-force face amount approximately $1.2T+ across the major mutual life carriers

products.name: Universal Life (UL)
products.brief_intro: Universal life combines a flexible-premium savings account with a death benefit. Premiums and death benefit can be adjusted within contractual limits. The account is credited interest above a contractual minimum; cost-of-insurance (COI) charges are deducted monthly.
products.description: Originally introduced by SSAP 51R / FAS 97 (now ASC 944-405). The account balance is the principal liability; COI and expense loads represent insurer revenue. Many UL contracts carry secondary guarantees (no-lapse UL or NLG) — the policy stays in force even if account balance drops to zero, provided minimum premiums were paid. Secondary-guarantee reserves under VM-20 can substantially exceed the account balance.
key_features: Flexible premium and adjustable death benefit
Account balance grows at credited rate (with contractual minimum)
Monthly COI charges scale with attained age
Surrender charges typically apply for first 10-20 years
products.market_note: US UL in-force ~$950B across major carriers including Lincoln, Pacific Life, Prudential, John Hancock

products.name: Variable Universal Life (VUL)
products.brief_intro: Variable universal life combines UL flexibility with separate-account investment funds chosen by the policyholder. Account performance reflects underlying-fund returns directly — the policyholder bears the market risk. Death benefit can be face-only or face-plus-account.
products.description: Issued by carriers like Lincoln, Prudential, Nationwide, AXA/Equitable. Separate accounts are presented at fair value on the balance sheet under ASC 944-80 / SSAP 56. The insurer retains contingent obligations through any guaranteed minimum death benefit (GMDB) rider, which is now an MRB under LDTI. SEC variable insurance products are also registered securities — dual-regulated by SEC and state insurance departments.
key_features: Policyholder selects from registered fund choices (typically 30-100 options)
Separate-account assets segregated from general account

products.name: Indexed Universal Life (IUL)
products.brief_intro: IUL credits the policyholder account based on a participation rate in an external index (typically S&P 500), subject to a cap and floor. The floor is typically 0% — policyholder never loses principal due to market drops, but participation is capped (e.g., 8-12%).
products.description: Hybrid product blending UL flexibility with bond-like floor + capped index participation. The embedded index-credit feature is typically bifurcated under ASC 815-15 as an embedded derivative measured at fair value through P&L, while the host UL contract continues at account balance. Carriers (Allianz Life, Nationwide, Pacific Life, John Hancock, Lincoln) hedge the index-credit obligation with S&P 500 call-option strategies.
key_features: Index-linked credited rate (S&P 500 typically) with cap and floor
Bifurcated embedded derivative for the index-credit feature
Persistency bonus or charge structures vary by carrier
products.market_note: US IUL annual premium grew ~10% CAGR 2018-2024; in-force ~$280B

products.name: Fixed Deferred Annuity
products.brief_intro: A deferred-annuity contract where the insurer credits a declared interest rate above a contractual minimum. The policyholder bears no market risk; the insurer earns the spread between investment yield and credited rate. Tax-deferred accumulation.
products.description: Pure investment-type contract — no significant mortality risk in the accumulation phase. Accounted for as a deposit (ASC 944 / SSAP 52). Statutory reserves under CARVM (SSAP 51R). Largest US fixed-annuity carriers include New York Life, MassMutual, Athene, MetLife, AIG. Many fixed annuities offer multi-year guaranteed-rate (MYGA) options locking in the credited rate.
key_features: Declared crediting rate above contractual minimum
products.market_note: US fixed-annuity in-force ~$600B; record 2023-2024 sales driven by elevated interest rates

products.name: Variable Annuity (VA)
products.brief_intro: Variable annuity offers tax-deferred investment in registered separate-account funds with optional living-benefit (GMxB) and death-benefit (GMDB) guarantees. Account performance reflects fund returns; guarantees create insurer obligations under stress scenarios.
products.description: Hybrid product carrying both investment characteristics and embedded insurance guarantees. Separate accounts at fair value (ASC 944-80 / SSAP 56). The GMxB riders — GMDB, GMAB, GMWB, GMIB — are Market Risk Benefits under LDTI (ASC 944-40-30-19A), measured at fair value with non-performance risk in OCI. Statutory reserves use VM-21 stochastic CTE-70 scenarios. Major writers: Equitable, Prudential, Brighthouse, Jackson, Lincoln.

products.name: Fixed Indexed Annuity (FIA)
products.brief_intro: FIA credits the contract based on participation in an external index (S&P 500, S&P MARC 5, custom volatility-controlled indices) with a floor of 0%. Principal is guaranteed against market drops. Surrender charges apply for first 7-12 years.
products.description: The dominant retail annuity product since 2018. Embedded index-credit feature is bifurcated as a derivative under ASC 815-15 and measured at fair value through P&L. Statutory reserves via CARVM. Major writers: Athene, Allianz Life, Equitable, AIG, F&G. Many FIAs include optional Guaranteed Lifetime Withdrawal Benefit (GLWB) riders for income certainty.
key_features: Indexed crediting with cap, participation rate, and floor (typically 0%)
Multiple crediting strategies (point-to-point, monthly cap, etc.)
Optional GLWB / GMWB rider for guaranteed income
Surrender charges 7-12 years; 10% free withdrawal typical
products.market_note: US FIA in-force ~$950B; annual sales above $90B since 2022

products.name: Pension Risk Transfer (PRT) — Buy-Out
products.brief_intro: In a PRT buy-out, an employer pension plan transfers the entire obligation to pay future pension benefits to an insurance company in exchange for a single premium. The plan is settled from the sponsor's perspective; the insurer pays retirees directly under group annuity contracts.
products.description: Booming market post-LDTI. Major writers: Prudential, MetLife, Athene, Pacific Life, Mass Mutual, RGA. Liabilities measured as LFPB under LDTI (ASC 944-40) at cohort level with annual unlocking. Statutory reserves under SSAP 51R / VM-22. Single-premium revenue recognized fully at contract inception; profit emerges over the lifetime as actual mortality experience unwinds the reserve. Deal sizes range from $50M to $20B+.
key_features: Sponsor exits from pension liability (full settlement)
May include lump-sum and continuing-annuity sub-cohorts
Frequently bundled with reinsurance to manage capital
products.market_note: US PRT premium written 2022-2024 averaged ~$50B/year; cumulative in-force ~$350B

products.name: Pension Risk Transfer (PRT) — Buy-In
products.brief_intro: A PRT buy-in is an insurance contract held by the pension plan as a plan asset. Unlike a buy-out, the plan does not settle the obligation — it holds the buy-in contract as an asset that exactly matches the benefit cash flows.
products.description: Useful as a step toward eventual buy-out, or as a risk-management overlay without triggering settlement accounting. The plan continues to pay retirees and the insurer reimburses the plan. From the insurer's perspective, identical accounting to a buy-out — LFPB under ASC 944-40. From the plan-sponsor perspective, the buy-in is a plan asset valued under ASC 715.
key_features: Insurance contract held by the plan as an asset
Plan continues to pay retirees; insurer reimburses
Does not trigger ASC 715 settlement accounting
Often a precursor to buy-out conversion
products.market_note: US PRT buy-in market is smaller than buy-out but growing as a transitional risk-management tool

products.name: Funding Agreement-Backed Notes (FABN / FABS)
products.brief_intro: FABNs are debt-like securities issued by a special-purpose entity backed by an insurance funding agreement. Used by life insurers to raise institutional capital at attractive funding costs while deploying proceeds into spread-based investments.
products.description: Major issuers include MetLife, New York Life, MassMutual, Pacific Life, Prudential, Athene, Brighthouse. Funding agreements are deposit-type contracts under SSAP 52 / ASC 944-405 — no insurance risk. The SPE issues registered notes (FABNs) to institutional buyers; proceeds are invested in spread-earning assets. The funding agreement is the SPE's offsetting asset. FABS-FHLB (Federal Home Loan Bank) advances are a related funding mechanism.
key_features: Funding agreement at insurer = deposit-type liability
SPE issues FABNs as registered debt to institutional buyers
FHLB advances are a related funding channel
products.market_note: US FABN / FHLB advance outstanding approximately $350B+

products.name: Guaranteed Investment Contract (GIC)
products.brief_intro: A GIC is a contract issued by a life insurer guaranteeing principal and a fixed (or floating) crediting rate over a stated maturity. Typically sold to retirement plans (401(k) stable-value options), corporate cash managers, and municipalities.
products.description: Deposit-type contract (SSAP 52 / ASC 944-405). Two flavors: traditional GIC (single-deposit, fixed rate, defined maturity) and synthetic GIC / stable-value wrap (insurer guarantees book value on a participant-directed investment portfolio). Major writers: New York Life, MetLife, Prudential, Pacific Life.
key_features: Traditional GIC: single deposit, fixed rate, maturity 1-5 years
Synthetic GIC: book-value wrap over participant-directed bond portfolio
products.market_note: US stable-value AUM ~$320B; GIC component approximately 60%

products.name: Homeowners Insurance
products.brief_intro: Multi-peril package covering dwelling, personal property, additional living expenses, and personal liability. The largest residential-property line in the US with approximately $130B in annual direct written premium.
products.description: Standard ISO HO-3 policy covers all perils except those excluded (most notably flood — separately insured via NFIP — and earthquake — separately insured). Premium recognized pro-rata under SSAP 53 / FAS 60 (ASC 944-605). Loss reserves under SSAP 55 / ASC 944-40 — undiscounted; case + IBNR + LAE. Property-catastrophe exposure managed through reinsurance and cat bonds.
key_features: Optional water-backup, scheduled jewelry, ordinance-and-law riders
products.market_note: US homeowners direct written premium ~$130B; largest writers: State Farm, Allstate, USAA, Liberty Mutual, Farmers, Travelers

products.name: Personal Auto Insurance
products.brief_intro: Personal auto is the largest P&C line in the US, with $300B+ in annual direct written premium. Covers liability (bodily injury, property damage), physical damage (comprehensive, collision), medical payments, and uninsured motorist.
products.description: Short-duration; premium earned pro-rata. The defining 2022-2024 industry challenge: severity inflation outpacing rate adequacy, driving combined ratios above 105% across major personal-auto writers. Reserve development typically modest in private auto due to short claim tail. Loss reserves under SSAP 55 / ASC 944-40.
key_features: Liability: bodily injury and property damage to others
products.market_note: US personal auto direct premium ~$320B; largest writers: State Farm, GEICO, Progressive, Allstate, USAA

products.name: Workers' Compensation
products.brief_intro: Workers' compensation pays indemnity and medical benefits to employees injured on the job, regardless of fault. Statutory in every US state (Texas optional). Long tail — indemnity claims can pay for decades.
products.description: Premium pro-rata earned (short-duration revenue) but loss reserves run to 30+ year tails for permanent-disability indemnity claims. Tabular discount permitted on indemnity tabular reserves with commissioner approval. Loss reserves under SSAP 55 / ASC 944-40. Schedule P loss-development analysis is critical for reserve adequacy. Major writers: Travelers, Liberty Mutual, AIG, Berkshire Hathaway, Zurich.
key_features: No-fault coverage with regulatory rate schedules
Heavy actuarial-specialist involvement under PCAOB AS 2501
products.market_note: US workers' comp direct premium ~$60B; competitive market with stable combined ratios sub-95%

products.name: General Liability (GL) / Commercial GL
products.brief_intro: Commercial general liability protects businesses against bodily-injury and property-damage claims arising from operations, products, and premises. Long tail similar to workers' comp due to occurrence-basis trigger and litigation timing.
products.description: Two primary coverage triggers: occurrence (claim payable if covered event occurred during policy period) and claims-made (claim payable if reported during policy period). Long-tail liabilities exposed to social inflation — jury verdicts trending higher have driven adverse development across the industry. Loss reserves under SSAP 55 / ASC 944-40; Schedule P disclosure critical.
kpis: Adverse development on prior accident years
products.market_note: US GL direct premium ~$70B; significant 2022-2024 adverse development on liability lines
